title: Map OptiSweep software data flow: OptiSweep → Ignition (OPC server) → AVEVA (HMI) and tippers via OPC
summary: Use the OptiSweep software stack mapping to identify where OPC-based communication originates (Ignition as the OPC server) and where data is consumed (AVEVA as the HMI). The source also states that Ignition communicates through the tippers via OPC and feeds data to AVEVA via direct OPC integration.
when_to_use: When you need to explain or reason about which layer is responsible for OPC-based communication and AVEVA data visibility, using the source-described responsibilities: Ignition as the OPC server (including OPC communication through the tippers) and AVEVA as the HMI consuming data via direct OPC integration.
not_for: Do not use this procedure as a live system troubleshooting guide for RMS/SSMS/WCS database state, because the packet does not provide live UI/DB/API check steps or commands for those systems.
roles_and_responsibilities: L1_support: Use the source-backed mapping to determine whether a reported AVEVA data visibility issue is more likely in the OPC server layer (Ignition) versus the HMI consumption layer (AVEVA), based on the responsibilities stated in the source.
access_or_tools_needed: Ability to reference the source-described software stack mapping (OptiSweep, AVEVA - HMI, Ignition - OPC Server, and the tippers via OPC) during troubleshooting discussions

visual_references.description: Training frame showing the OptiSweep software stack labels including “Aveva - HMI” and “Ignition - OPC Server”, and the described communication/data flow.

steps.title: Review the OptiSweep software stack mapping (OptiSweep, Ignition - OPC Server, AVEVA - HMI)
steps.purpose: Establish the source-described component responsibilities so you can attribute OPC communication and AVEVA data consumption to the correct layer during troubleshooting.
steps.instruction: Use the source-described stack mapping: OptiSweep integrates the system; Ignition is the OPC server; AVEVA is the HMI. When discussing the mapping, reference the labeled components shown in the source frame.
steps.expected_result: You can state (based on the source mapping) that Ignition is the OPC server and AVEVA is the HMI in the OptiSweep software stack.
steps.healthy_condition: The mapping you use in the troubleshooting discussion matches the source labels: “Ignition - OPC Server” and “Aveva - HMI”.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot correctly identify which component is the OPC server (Ignition) versus the HMI consumer (AVEVA) per the source mapping.

actions.label: Confirm stack labels
actions.exact_action: Review the labeled software stack components: “Aveva - HMI” and “Ignition - OPC Server”.

steps.title: Confirm the OPC communication path: Ignition communicates through the tippers via OPC
steps.purpose: Determine where OPC-based communication originates so you can reason about whether an issue is likely in the OPC server layer.
steps.instruction: Use the source-described responsibility that Ignition communicates through the tippers through OPC.
steps.expected_result: You can state that Ignition is the component that communicates through the tippers via OPC.
steps.healthy_condition: Your troubleshooting attribution for OPC communication points to Ignition (OPC server) rather than AVEVA.
steps.failure_condition: You attribute OPC communication through the tippers to AVEVA or to a component other than Ignition, contradicting the source mapping.

actions.label: Confirm OPC-through-tippers statement
actions.exact_action: Use the source statement that Ignition “communicates through the tippers through OPC”.

steps.title: Confirm the data consumption path: Ignition feeds data to AVEVA via direct OPC integration
steps.purpose: Determine where AVEVA gets its data so you can reason about whether an issue is more likely in the OPC server layer (Ignition) versus the HMI consumption layer (AVEVA).
steps.instruction: Use the source-described responsibility that Ignition feeds data to AVEVA because AVEVA can directly integrate with the OPC server.
steps.expected_result: You can state that Ignition feeds data to AVEVA and that AVEVA integrates directly with the OPC server.
steps.healthy_condition: Your troubleshooting attribution for AVEVA data visibility points to the OPC server layer (Ignition) for OPC delivery and to AVEVA for HMI consumption, consistent with the source mapping.
steps.failure_condition: You cannot explain how AVEVA receives data (per the source) or you claim AVEVA does not integrate with the OPC server.

actions.label: Confirm AVEVA direct OPC integration statement
actions.exact_action: Use the source statement that Ignition “also feeds data to AVEVA since they can directly integrate with our OPC server.”

stop_or_escalate_if: If live system evidence contradicts the source mapping (e.g., AVEVA is not integrating with the OPC server as described), stop and escalate for deeper system-specific investigation.

steps.title: Use the mapping to guide troubleshooting attribution for AVEVA data visibility issues (Ignition vs AVEVA layer)
steps.purpose: Provide a source-grounded decision rule for where to look first when AVEVA does not show expected data.
steps.instruction: When AVEVA data visibility is reported, use the source-described responsibilities to state whether the issue is more likely in the OPC server layer (Ignition) versus the HMI consumption layer (AVEVA): Ignition is responsible for OPC communication (including through the tippers) and feeding data to AVEVA; AVEVA is the HMI that integrates directly with the OPC server.
steps.expected_result: You can articulate a source-backed attribution: OPC delivery/communication issues are more likely in Ignition (OPC server), while HMI consumption/integration issues are more likely in AVEVA.
steps.healthy_condition: Your troubleshooting discussion clearly distinguishes the OPC server layer (Ignition) from the HMI consumption layer (AVEVA) using the source responsibilities.
steps.failure_condition: Your troubleshooting attribution does not distinguish between Ignition (OPC server) and AVEVA (HMI), or contradicts the source responsibilities.

actions.label: State likely layer using responsibilities
actions.exact_action: Use the source mapping: Ignition is the OPC server that communicates through the tippers via OPC and feeds data to AVEVA; AVEVA integrates directly with the OPC server.

stop_or_escalate_if: If live system evidence contradicts the source mapping, stop and escalate for deeper system-specific investigation.

success_criteria: You can correctly identify Ignition as the OPC server and AVEVA as the HMI consumer per the source mapping.
You can correctly explain that Ignition communicates through the tippers via OPC and feeds data to AVEVA via direct OPC integration.
For an AVEVA data visibility issue, you can provide a source-grounded attribution of likely layer (Ignition vs AVEVA) without contradicting the source responsibilities.
healthy_conditions: Troubleshooting explanations consistently reference Ignition as the OPC server and AVEVA as the HMI, and distinguish OPC communication/feeding from HMI consumption.
failure_conditions: Attribution contradicts the source mapping (e.g., claiming AVEVA is the OPC server or that AVEVA does not integrate with the OPC server).
Live evidence contradicts the source mapping; escalation is required.
escalation_guidance: If live system evidence contradicts the source mapping (e.g., AVEVA is not integrating with the OPC server as described), stop and escalate for deeper system-specific investigation.
missing_details: The packet does not provide live AVEVA UI checks, Ignition OPC server status checks, or any commands/queries to validate OPC connectivity or data points on the running system.

The packet does not specify which exact AVEVA screens/tags correspond to which OPC items, so the runbook cannot map a specific missing AVEVA display to a specific OPC server component beyond the layer attribution.
